      INITIAL BRIEF OF INTERVENOR ALISON BECHTER (TRACT 3510)
         Post-Hearing Initial Brief Following the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

Intervenor Alison Bechter ("Ms. Bechter" or "Intervenor"), appearing pro se as the intervenor of
record for Tract 3510, respectfully submits this Initial Brief following the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing
on the Merits in the above-styled and -numbered proceeding, and would respectfully show the
Administrative Law Judges ("ALJs") the following.


I. STATEMENT OF THE CASE AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY
This proceeding concerns the joint application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC ("Oncor'')
and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation ("LCRA TSC," and together with Oncor,
"Applicants") to amend their respective Certificates of Convenience and Necessity ("CCN") to
construct, own, and operate the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kV
Transmission Line Project (the "Project"). Among the alternative routes presented for the
Commission's consideration are Segment A2, an alignment that would cross or closely approach
Intervenor's property, and Segment A3, an alternative alignment that would avoid Intervenor's
property and the immediately surrounding rural community. Notably, Applicants' own Initial Post-
Hearing Brief, filed in this docket on June 19, 2026, does not advocate for the selection of
Segment A2 or any other specific route; it states that "Applicants do not object to the selection of
any filed route or constructible combination of forward-progressing alternative route links," and
that Applicants will construct whatever route the Commission selects among the 122 routes
presented in the Application.

Ms. Bechter is the owner of Tract 3510, a ten-acre parcel located adjacent to the residential
property at 8564 Shaw Road, Rogers, Texas 76569, in Bell County, where she also resides. Ms.
Bechter intervened in this proceeding in her individual capacity as the owner of Tract 3510. Her
husband, Aaron C. Bechter, is a separate, independently-represented pro se intervenor of record
with respect to Tract 3509, the adjoining residential property. Ms. Bechter and Mr. Bechter have
filed separate testimony, separate exhibits, and separate briefing in this docket, and each relies
on his or her own personal knowledge of his or her own tract. This Brief addresses only Ms.
Bechter's position as to Tract 3510.


PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Alison Bechter    Page 1 of 8
 Ms. Bechter filed her Direct Testimony and Statement of Position in this docket in advance of the
Commission's prefiled testimony deadline. Applicants thereafter filed objections to, and a motion
to strike, portions of the prefiled testimony of multiple intervenors, including Ms. Bechter. Ms.
Bechter timely filed her Response to Applicants' Objections to and Motion to Strike Intervenor
Testimony on May 26, 2026, consistent with the response deadline established under 16 Tex.
Admin. Code § 22. 78, as expressly acknowledged on the record by counsel for LCRA TSC. On
June 3, 2026, Ms. Bechter filed her Prehearing Exhibit List (Exhibits A through M) and Witness
List, identifying herself as her own sole witness. Following the June 5, 2026 prehearing
conference, the ALJs convened a Hearing on the Merits, which proceeded from June 8 through
June 12, 2026.

During the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits, the ALJs denied Applicants' Motion to Strike
in its entirety. Ms. Bechter's Direct Testimony and Statement of Position was admitted into the
evidentiary record as filed, without change, limitation, or redaction. Her exhibits - including
Exhibits G, H, and M, which are letters from Texas state legislators placing the Commission on
notice of landowner and community concerns regarding the Project, offered for the limited, non-
hearsay purpose of establishing notice to the Commission rather than the truth of the matters
asserted therein -were likewise admitted. Applicants' counsel did not press a hearsay or other
objection to those exhibits at hearing. Ms. Bechter was not called for cross-examination by any
party. Her Direct Testimony and exhibits therefore stand in the record unrebutted.

Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6 and SOAH Order No. 32 (Addressing Post-Hearing Matters, Jun.
15, 2026), Initial Briefs are due no later than 11:59 p.m. Central Time on June 19, 2026, with
Reply Briefs and Proposed Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Ordering Paragraphs due
June 26, 2026. Ms. Bechter timely files this Initial Brief in accordance with that schedule.


II. SUMMARY OF ARGUMENT
Applicants bear the burden of proving, by a preponderance of the evidence, that Segment A2 is
necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public under PURA §
37.056(a), and that the routing of Segment A2 properly accounts for the factors enumerated in
PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (b)(3)(B), including community values,
environmental integrity, and the Commission's policy of prudent avoidance.

The unrebutted record contains sworn testimony establishing concrete, and in significant part
irreversible, harm to Ms. Bechter from Segment A2 as proposed. Most significantly, Tract 3510 is
two years into the five-year consecutive qualification period required under Texas law for an
agricultural property tax exemption. Construction activity associated with Segment A2 threatens
to interrupt the continuity of qualifying agricultural use on the parcel, which would require Ms.
Bechter to restart that five-year clock and would expose her to back-tax liability- a quantifiable,
present, and ongoing financial harm, not a speculative future one.

Applicants offered no evidence at hearing controverting Ms. Bechter's testimony, and no evidence
explaining why Segment A2, rather than Segment A3 or another alignment that avoids Tract 3510,
best satisfies the statutory and regulatory routing criteria. The disproportion in landowner



PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Alison Bechter   Page 2 of 8
 opposition is itself probative: by Intervenor's review of the Commission's docket activity in this
proceeding, approximately twenty-four landowners have intervened in opposition to alignments
along Segment A2, compared to a single intervenor or protestant associated with Segment A3.
That disparity bears directly on the "community values" and impact-moderation factors the
Commission must weigh under PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code§ 25.101 (b)(3)(B).

Because Applicants have not carried their burden as to Segment A2, and because the unrebutted
record establishes that a materially less-impactful alternative remains available, the Commission
should decline to approve Segment A2 to the extent it affects Tract 3510, and should give full and
serious weight to Segment A3 or any alignment that avoids Ms. Bechter's property.


Ill. BURDEN OF PROOF AND STANDARD OF REVIEW
Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA"), the Commission "may approve an application
and grant a certificate only if the commission finds that the certificate is necessary for the service,
accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public." PURA § 37.056(a) (Tex. Util. Code Ann.§
37.056(a)). In making that determination, and in particular in selecting among alternative routes,
the Commission must consider the factors set out in PURA § 37.056(c), including the adequacy
of existing service, the need for additional service, and "other factors, such as (A) community
values; (B) recreational and park areas; (C) historical and aesthetic values; [and] (D)
environmental integrity." PURA § 37.056(c)(4). The Commission's own substantive rule
implementing these statutory routing factors, 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (b)(3)(B), further
requires consideration of whether a proposed route uses or parallels existing compatible rights-
of-way, whether it parallels property lines or natural or cultural features, and whether it conforms
with the Commission's policy of "prudent avoidance" - defined under 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
25.101 (a)(6) as "the limiting of exposures to electric and magnetic fields that can be avoided with
reasonable investments of money and effort." These factors "are stated in the broadest possible
terms and are intended as legislative standards to guide the Commission in its administration of
the certification process," to be considered only in the context of the case at hand and weighed
against one another where they compete. Hammack v. Pub. Util. Comm'n of Tex., 131 S.W.3d
713,719,723,727 (Tex. App.-Austin 2004); Pub. Util. Comm'n v. Texland Elec. Co., 701 S.W.2d
261,266 (Tex. App.-Austin 1985); see also Dunn v. Pub. Util. Comm'n of Tex., 246 S.W.3d 788,
794 (Tex. App.-Austin 2008).

As the parties seeking affirmative relief and seeking to change the status quo by obtaining
authority to construct new 765-kV transmission infrastructure across private property that does
not presently host such infrastructure, Applicants bear the burden of proof in this proceeding. See
1 Tex. Admin. Code § 155.427 (identifying the party seeking affirmative relief and the party
seeking to change the status quo as the party ordinarily bearing the burden of proof in SOAH
contested-case proceedings). That burden must be carried by a preponderance of the evidence.
See Granek v. Tex. State Bd. of Med. Exam'rs, 172 S.W.3d 761, 777 (Tex. App.-Austin 2005,
no pet.). Where, as here, Applicants offered no evidence at hearing rebutting an intervenor's
sworn, unchallenged testimony of specific and concrete harm, and offered no comparative routing
evidence addressing that harm, the preponderance standard is not met as to the route segment
affecting that intervenor's property.


PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Alison Bechter     Page 3 of 8
 IV. STATEMENT OF FACTS- EVIDENCE OF RECORD

A. Intervenor's Standing and Property

Ms. Bechter owns Tract 3510, a ten-acre parcel adjacent to the residential property at 8564 Shaw
Road, Rogers, Texas, where she resides with her husband. Her standing in this proceeding rests
on her ownership of Tract 3510 and on her personal, firsthand knowledge of the agricultural use,
character, and conditions of that property, as set forth in her Direct Testimony and Statement of
Position, admitted into evidence during the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits without
limitation.

B. Proximity of Proposed Segment A2

As established in Ms. Bechter's admitted Direct Testimony and supporting exhibits, the structures
proposed for Segment A2 would be located approximately 1,519.49 feet from Tract 3510. This
measurement is based on Ms. Bechter's personal review of Applicants' own routing materials and
publicly available mapping data, and is unrebutted in the record.

C. Current Agricultural Use
Ms. Bechter currently raises chickens on Tract 3510. The adjoining residential tract maintains an
active agricultural property tax exemption based on hay production, which directly supports and
reinforces the rural, working-land character of Tract 3510 itself.

D. The Agricultural Exemption Qualification Period
Tract 3510 is, as of the date of this Brief, two years into the five-year period of continuous,
qualifying agricultural use required under Texas law to establish an agricultural property tax
exemption (commonly referred to as an "ag exemption") on the parcel. This qualification period
must run consecutively; an interruption in qualifying use during the five-year window requires the
landowner to begin the qualification period anew. Construction activity, easement clearing,
access-road construction, and the operational presence of 765-kV transmission infrastructure
associated with Segment A2 each threaten to interrupt the continuity of Ms. Bechter's qualifying
agricultural use on Tract 3510. Unlike many of the impacts addressed in this proceeding, this
harm is not speculative or contingent on future events outside Applicants' control - it is a direct,
foreseeable, and quantifiable consequence of construction proceeding through or immediately
adjacent to Tract 3510 during the pendency of the qualification period, and it is unrebutted in the
record.

E. Planned Agricultural Expansion
Ms. Bechter has concrete, specific plans- not speculative or aspirational ones- to expand her
agricultural operations on Tract 3510 to include cattle grazing and beekeeping. These plans form
part of the basis for, and are integral to, her ongoing efforts to complete the five-year agricultural-
use qualification period described above. Bees in particular are recognized as sensitive to
construction disturbance and to changes in their immediate environment, a consideration directly




PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Alison Bechter     Page 4 of 8
 relevant to the Commission's prudent-avoidance analysis under 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
25.101 (a)(6) given the proximity of the proposed Segment A2 structures to Tract 3510.

F. Survey and Access Activity

Ms. Bechter personally observed unexplained survey and access activity on or near her property
on or about March 2, 2025, and again on or about April2, 2025. Applicants were unable to provide
Ms. Bechter with a satisfactory explanation for this activity at the time it occurred. This testimony
is based on Ms. Bechter's direct, firsthand observation and is unrebutted.

G. Rural Character, Environmental, and Cumulative Impact
Ms. Bechter has personally observed the cumulative industrialization of the rural corridor
surrounding Tract 3510, including nearby solar development, associated road degradation,
displacement of wildlife, and increased coyote activity in the immediate vicinity of her property.
These firsthand observations are relevant to the "environmental integrity" and "community values"
factors the Commission must weigh under PURA § 37.056(c)(4), and they establish that Segment
A2 would not be imposed on an undisturbed rural landscape, but on a community already
absorbing substantial cumulative energy-infrastructure impact.

H. Notice to the Commission -         Admitted Legislative Correspondence

Exhibits G, H, and M, admitted during the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits, consist of
letters submitted to the Commission by Texas state legislators - dated April 29, 2026, May 5,
2026, and May 11, 2026, respectively - documenting legislative concern regarding the Project
and the broader pace of the Commission's review of proposed 765-kV transmission infrastructure
across the affected region. These exhibits were, and remain, offered solely for the limited, non-
hearsay purpose of establishing that the Commission has been placed on formal notice of these
concerns, not for the truth of the matters asserted in them. Their admission without sustained
objection confirms that this is properly part of the evidentiary record before the Commission in
evaluating the public-interest and community-values factors applicable to this proceeding.


V.ARGUMENT

A. Applicants Have Not Carried Their Burden Under PURA § 37.056 as to Segment A2

PURA § 37.056(a) permits the Commission to grant the requested CCN amendment only upon a
finding that it is necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public.
That finding, where the application presents multiple route alternatives, necessarily requires the
Commission to evaluate whether the specific route selected - here, Segment A2 - reflects
appropriate consideration of the factors in PURA § 37.056(c), including community values and
environmental integrity. Applicants presented no evidence during the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing
on the Merits rebutting Ms. Bechter's unchallenged testimony regarding the concrete harm
Segment A2 would impose on Tract 3510, and no evidence explaining why that harm is
outweighed by any corresponding benefit specific to the A2 alignment as opposed to Segment
A3 or another route that avoids Tract 3510. Indeed, Applicants' own Initial Post-Hearing Brief



PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Alison Bechter    Page 5 of 8
 confirms that they press no such case: Applicants ask the ALJs to recommend approval "along
any filed route" and state that they "do not object to the selection of any filed route or constructible
combination of forward-progressing alternative route links." Applicants having declined to defend
Segment A2 specifically, there is no evidentiary or argumentative basis in this record on which
the Commission could find that Segment A2, rather than Segment A3 or another alignment
avoiding Tract 3510, satisfies PURA § 37.056(c). On this record, Applicants have not carried their
burden by a preponderance of the evidence as to Segment A2 insofar as it affects Tract 3510.

B. The Routing Criteria of 16 Tex. Admin. Code§ 25.101(b)(3)(B) Do Not Favor Segment
A2 Over an Alignment That Avoids Tract 3510
Section 25.101 (b)(3)(B) directs the Commission to consider, among other things, whether a route
conforms with the policy of prudent avoidance. Prudent avoidance does not require routing
decisions to eliminate all proximity between transmission infrastructure and private property; it
requires the Commission to favor reasonable, available alternatives that limit exposure and impact
"with reasonable investments of money and effort." 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (a)(6). The
Commission has previously found that prudent avoidance is achieved by minimizing the number
of habitable structures located in close proximity to a proposed route, see Joint Application of
Elec. Transmission Tex., LLC & Sharyland Utils. to Amend Their CCNs for the North Edinburg to
Lema Alta Double-Circuit 345-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 41606, FOF No. 64 (Apr. 11,
2011 ), and that routing along property boundaries or fencelines while avoiding habitable
structures helps preserve the community values and recreational-area factors that PURA §
37.056(c) requires the Commission to weigh. See Application of Brazos Elec. Power Coop., Inc.
to Amend a CCN for a Proposed Transmission Line Within Cooke Cnty., Docket No. 20516, FOF
No. 85 (Jan. 26, 2001 ). Here, a reasonable, already-identified alternative- Segment A3- exists
and is before the Commission in this same proceeding. Applicants have not shown, by evidence
presented at hearing, why selecting that reasonable alternative, or another alignment that avoids
Tract 3510, would not satisfy the public need that Applicants assert while materially reducing the
impact on Ms. Bechter and the surrounding community.

C. The Disparity in Landowner Opposition Confirms Segment A2 Fails to Moderate
Impact on the Affected Community
The "community values" factor under PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A) is not an abstraction; the
Commission has defined it as "a shared appreciation of an area or other mutual resource by a
national, regional, or local community," with adverse effects consisting of "those aspects of a
proposed project that would significantly alter the use, enjoyment, or intrinsic value attached to
an important area or resource by a community." Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Round Rock-Leander 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 45866,
Order on Rehearing, FOF No. 37 (Jul. 28, 2017); Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Proposed EC Mornhinweg to Parkway 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket
No. 40684, FOF 43 (Jun. 19, 2013). That impact is measured, in part, by the lived response of
the community to the route as proposed. By Intervenor's review of the Commission's docket
activity in this proceeding, approximately twenty-four landowners have intervened in opposition
to alignments along Segment A2, while only a single intervenor or protestant is associated with
Segment A3. Intervenor recognizes that, pursuant to SOAH Order No. 24 (Ruling on Intervenor


PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Alison Bechter       Page 6 of 8
 Motions, Granting Leave for Late-Filed Testimonies, and Dismissing Intervenors, Jun. 1, 2026),
a substantial number of intervenors in this large, fifteen-county proceeding were dismissed for
procedural reasons unrelated to the merits of their concerns; that history does not diminish the
relevance of the disparity among the intervenors who remained eligible to participate at hearing,
but Intervenor respectfully requests that the Commission independently confirm the precise
figures from its own docket records. The Commission should take into account the magnitude of
this disparity, as it bears directly and substantially on whether Segment A2, as proposed, reflects
the degree of community-impact moderation that PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code§
25.101 (b)(3)(B) require. This conclusion is consistent with the position of the Office of Public Utility
Counsel, which in its own Post-Hearing Initial Brief filed in this docket on June 18, 2026, urged
the Commission to scrutinize this application "with the aim of having the fewest number of
landowners ... affected by approval of this project," and to give the concerns raised by pro se
intervenors equal footing with those raised by represented parties.

D. Prudent Avoidance Requires Particular Care Where the Harm Is Concrete and Partially
Irreversible

Most of the impacts addressed in this proceeding are properly characterized as ongoing or
prospective. The harm to Ms. Bechter's agricultural-exemption qualification period is different in
kind: it is presently accruing, it is time-bound, and an interruption caused by Segment A2
construction cannot later be undone by post-hoc mitigation - the five-year consecutive
qualification period would simply have to begin again. This is precisely the type of concrete,
quantifiable harm that the Commission's prudent-avoidance policy is designed to weigh against
the burden of selecting a reasonable alternative alignment. Because that alternative exists and is
before the Commission in this docket, prudent avoidance counsels against approving Segment
A2 as it affects Tract 3510.

E. The Record Evidence of Mounting Legislative Concern Supports a Cautious, Fully-
Informed Routing Decision
Exhibits G, H, and M- properly admitted at hearing for the limited purpose of establishing notice
to the Commission - demonstrate that elected representatives of the affected region have, over
a period of weeks, repeatedly and formally communicated concern to the Commission regarding
the pace and scope of review applicable to this and related 765-kV transmission proposals. While
these exhibits are not offered for the truth of the specific factual assertions they contain, their
admission confirms that the Commission has been placed on notice, through its own docket, that
the routing decision in this proceeding is one of substantial and growing public and legislative
concern - reinforcing the importance of a full and careful application of the statutory and
regulatory routing criteria before approving Segment A2.


VI. CONCLUSION AND PRAYER FOR RELIEF
For the foregoing reasons, Intervenor Alison Bechter respectfully requests that the Administrative
Law Judges find and recommend, and that the Commission ultimately determine, that Applicants
have not met their burden under PURA § 37.056 to show that Segment A2 is necessary for the
service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public insofar as that segment affects


PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Alison Bechter       Page 7 of 8
 Tract 3510. Ms. Bechter further requests that the Commission decline to approve Segment A2 as
it affects Tract 3510, and instead give full and serious weight to Segment A3, or to any alternative
alignment that avoids Tract 3510, consistent with the Commission's policy of prudent avoidance
and the routing criteria of PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (b)(3)(8). Ms.
Bechter's ultimate position is, and has consistently been, opposition to the physical proximity of
765-kV transmission infrastructure to Tract 3510- not opposition to any particular segment label
- and she requests that any route the Commission ultimately approves avoid her property.

In the alternative, should the Commission nonetheless approve Segment A2 in a manner that
affects Tract 3510, Ms. Bechter respectfully requests that the Commission order implementation
of optimum phasing and any other reasonable, available mitigation measures the Commission
has required in prior dockets to minimize electric and magnetic field exposure and other impacts
to the parcel, consistent with the Commission's policy of prudent avoidance. See, e.g., Application
of Cross Tex. Transmission, LLC to Amend its CCN for the Limestone to Gibbons Creek 345-kV
Transmission Line, Docket No. 44649, FOF No. 237 (Jan. 13, 2016). Ms. Bechterfurther requests
such other and further relief, at law or in equity, to which she may show herself justly entitled.


Respectfully submitted,



Alison Bechter
Intervenor, Pro Se- Tract 3510
8564 Shaw Road, Rogers, Texas 76569
PUC Docket No. 59475/ SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
Date: June 19, 2026


CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I certify that a true and correct copy of the foregoing Initial Brief has been served on all parties of
record in this proceeding in accordance with the orders and procedural rules applicable to PUC
Docket No. 59475 and SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, on this 19th day of June, 2026 .

Ill. BURDEN OF PROOF AND STANDARD OF REVIEW
Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA'), the Commission "may approve an application
and grant a certificate only if the commission finds that the certificate is necessary for the service,
accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public." PURA § 37.056(a) (Tex. Util. Code Ann. §
37.056(a)). In making that determination, and in particular in selecting among alternative routes,
the Commission must consider the factors set out in PURA § 37.056(c), including the adequacy
of existing service, the need for additional service, and 'other factors, such as (A) community
values; (B) recreational and park areas; (C) historical and aesthetic values; [and] (D)
environmental integrity." PURA § 37.056(c)(4). The Commission's own substantive rule
implementing these statutory routing factors, 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B), further
requires consideration of whether a proposed route uses or parallels existing compatible rights-
of-way, whether it parallels property lines or natural or cultural features, and whether it conforms
with the Commission's policy of £'prudent avoidance" - defined under 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
25.101(a)(6) as "the limiting of exposures to electric and magnetic fields that can be avoided with
reasonable investments of money and effort." These factors "are stated in the broadest possible
terms and are intended as legislative standards to guide the Commission in its administration of
the certification process," to be considered only in the context of the case at hand and weighed
against one another where they compete. Hammack v. Pub. Util. Comm'n of Tex., 131 S.W.3d
713, 719, 723, 727 (Tex. App.-Austin 2004); Pub. Util. Comm'n v. Texland Elec. Co., 701 S.W.2d
261, 266 (Tex. App.-Austin 1985); see also Dunn v. Pub. Util. Comm'n of Tex., 246 S.W.3d 788,
794 (Tex. App.-Austin 2008).

As the parties seeking affirmative relief and seeking to change the status quo by obtaining
authority to construct new 765-kV transmission infrastructure across private property that does
not presently host such infrastructure, Applicants bear the burden of proof in this proceeding. See
1 Tex. Admin. Code § 155.427 (identifying the party seeking affirmative relief and the party
seeking to change the status quo as the party ordinarily bearing the burden of proof in SOAH
contested-case proceedings). That burden must be carried by a preponderance of the evidence.
See Granek v. Tex. State Bd. of Med. Exam'rs, 172 S.W.3d 761, 777 (Tex. App.-Austin 2005,
no pet.). Where, as here, Applicants offered no evidence at hearing rebutting an intervenor's
sworn, unchallenged testimony of specific and concrete harm, and offered no comparative routing
evidence addressing that harm, the preponderance standard is not met as to the route segment
affecting that intervenor's property.

V. ARGUMENT
A. Applicants Have Not Carried Their Burden Under PURA § 37.056 as to Segment A2
PURA § 37.056(a) permits the Commission to grant the requested CCN amendment only upon a
finding that it is necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public.
That finding, where the application presents multiple route alternatives, necessarily requires the
Commission to evaluate whether the specific route selected - here, Segment A2 - reflects
appropriate consideration of the factors in PURA § 37.056(c), including community values and
environmental integrity. Applicants presented no evidence during the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing
on the Merits rebutting Ms. Bechtefs unchallenged testimony regarding the concrete harm
Segment A2 would impose on Tract 3510, and no evidence explaining why that harm is
outweighed by any corresponding benefit specific to the A2 alignment as opposed to Segment
A3 or another route that avoids Tract 3510. Indeed, Applicants' own Initial Post-Hearing Brief

 confirms that they press no such case: Applicants ask the ALJs to recommend approval "along
any filed route" and state that they "do not object to the selection of any filed route or constructible
combination of forward-progressing alternative route links." Applicants having declined to defend
Segment A2 specifically, there is no evidentiary or argumentative basis in this record on which
the Commission could find that Segment A2, rather than Segment A3 or another alignment
avoiding Tract 3510, satisfies PURA § 37.056(c). On this record, Applicants have not carried their
burden by a preponderance of the evidence as to Segment A2 insofar as it affeds Tract 3510.

B. The Routing Criteria of 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B) Do Not Favor Segment
A2 Over an Alignment That Avoids Tract 3510
Section 25.101(b)(3)(B) directs the Commission to consider, among other things, whether a route
conforms with the policy of prudent avoidance. Prudent avoidance does not require routing
decisions to eliminate all proximity between transmission infrastructure and private property; it
requires the Commission to favor reasonable, available alternatives that limit exposure and impact
"with reasonable investments of money and effort." 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(a)(6). The
Commission has previously found that prudent avoidance is achieved by minimizing the number
of habitable structures located in close proximity to a proposed route, see Joint Application of
Elec. Transmission Tex., LLC & Sharyland Utils. to Amend Their CCNs for the North Edinburg to
Loma Alta Double-Circuit 345-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 41606, FOF No. 64 (Apr. 11,
2011), and that routing along property boundaries or fencelines while avoiding habitable
structures helps preserve the community values and recreational-area factors that PURA §
37.056(c) requires the Commission to weigh. See Application of Brazos Elec. Power Coop., Inc.
to Amend a CCN for a Proposed Transmission Line Within Cooke Cnty., Docket No. 20516, FOF
No. 85 (Jan. 26,2001). Here, a reasonable, already-identified alternative - Segment A3 - exists
and is before the Commission in this same proceeding. Applicants have not shown, by evidence
presented at hearing, why selecting that reasonable alternative, or another alignment that avoids
Tract 3510, would not satisfy the public need that Applicants assert while materially reducing the
impact on Ms. Bechter and the surrounding community.

C. The Disparity in Landowner Opposition Confirms Segment A2 Fails to Moderate
Impact on the Affected Community
The "community values" factor under PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A) is not an abstraction; the
Commission has defined it as "a shared appreciation of an area or other mutual resource by a
national, regional, or local community," with adverse effects consisting of "those aspects of a
proposed project that would significantly alter the use, enjoyment, or intrinsic value attached to
an important area or resource by a community." Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Round Rock-Leander 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 45866,
Order on Rehearing, FOF No. 37 (Jul. 28, 2017); Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Proposed EC Mornhinweg to Parkway 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket
No. 40684, FOF 43 (Jun. 19, 2013). That impact is measured, in part, by the lived response of
the community to the route as proposed. By Intervenor's review of the Commission's docket
activity in this proceeding, approximately twenty-four landowners have intervened in opposition
to alignments along Segment A2, while only a single intervenor or protestant is associated with
Segment A3. Intervenor recognizes that, pursuant to SOAH Order No. 24 (Ruling on Intervenor

D. Prudent Avoidance Requires Particular Care Where the Harm Is Concrete and Partially
Irreversible
Most of the impacts addressed in this proceeding are properly characterized as ongoing or
prospective. The harm to Ms. Bechter's agricultural-exemption qualification period is different in
kind: it is presently accruing, it is time-bound, and an interruption caused by Segment A2
construction cannot later be undone by post-hoc mitigation - the five-year consecutive
qualification period would simply have to begin again. This is precisely the type of concrete,
quantifiable harm that the Commission's prudent-avoidance policy is designed to weigh against
the burden of selecting a reasonable alternative alignment. Because that alternative exists and is
before the Commission in this docket, prudent avoidance counsels against approving Segment
A2 as it affects Tract 3510.

E. The Record Evidence of Mounting Legislative Concern Supports a Cautious, Fully-

Exhibits G, H, and M - properly admitted at hearing for the limited purpose of establishing notice
